items.title: Continuum body data, the fixed inertial frame and the dimensions of the fields
items.design_state: authored; step-1 readiness recorded in the batch notes
items.physical_scope: The kinematic and dimensional framework of the continuum branch: one fixed inertial frame, a reference material region with a reference chart domain, a time window, and the dimensions of the density, velocity, acceleration, body-force, traction, stress, displacement, elastic, viscous, pressure and wave-speed fields. The definition fixes conventions only; it asserts no motion, no balance law, no constitutive relation and no measured value.

items.statement:
**(a) Framework and frame.** The framework is the non-relativistic classical
mechanics of [[post-cm01-spacetime]] with the inertial frames, stationary
observers and allowed changes of frame of [[post-cm01-frames]]; the particle
worldline conventions of [[post-cm01-worldlines]] are used for the labeled
points of a body, and dimensions and reference units (metre, second, kilogram)
are read by [[def-cm01-units]]. Throughout this page one inertial frame $F$
with adapted coordinates $(t,x)$ of the affine time space
[[def-cm-affine-time-space]] is fixed, and each simultaneous spatial slice is
identified with $\mathbb R^3$ carrying its standard Euclidean structure. The
time coordinate $t$ is the model's time in seconds, $[t]=\tau$, and the
spatial components $x_i$ are positions in metres, $[x_i]=\ell$. All fields
below are read in this one frame.

consisting of

3. a nonempty open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$, the **time window**

items.title: Adopted continuum kinematic model: body data, smooth motions as families of label worldlines, the continuum idealization and frame covariance
items.design_state: authored; step-1 readiness recorded in the batch notes
items.physical_scope: Adoption of the kinematic branch of the continuum framework: every model is carried by body data in a fixed inertial frame; the body's motion is a C^2 family of orientation-preserving injective configurations whose labels follow worldlines and whose velocity field carries the model's spatial velocity and material acceleration; the continuum hypothesis, the smoothness idealization and the frame-covariance requirement are stated. The postulate excludes fracture, interpenetration, phase boundaries, shocks, diffusion, chemical reactions and thermal or electromagnetic coupling, and asserts no dynamics, no constitutive relation and no measured value.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the continuum branch the following statements,
in the framework, frame and body data of [[def-cm17-continuum-body-and-units]].

**(i) Model data.** A model of the branch is carried by a continuum body data
set $(B,O,I)$ of [[def-cm17-continuum-body-and-units]] in the fixed inertial
frame $F$: a material region $B$, a reference chart domain $O$ with
$\overline B\subseteq O$, and a time window $I$. The labels $X\in B$ are the
material points of the body.

**(ii) Motion.** A **motion** of the model is a map

$$\chi:I\times O\longrightarrow\mathbb R^3$$

which is a motion of the material region $B$ on $I$ in the sense of
[[def-cm-continuum-motion]]: $\chi$ is of class $C^2$; for every $t\in I$ the

total derivative at every point of $O$; and the Jacobian

current region is $\Omega_t:=\chi_t(B)$, and the model's **spatial velocity
field** $u$ and **material acceleration** $a=D_tu$ are those of

items.title: The density field of the continuum model and the mass of a material subregion
items.design_state: authored; step-1 readiness recorded in the batch notes
items.physical_scope: The density field of a continuum model, its dimensions (mass per unit volume), and the model's mass of a material subregion at a given time, computed as the Lebesgue integral of the density over the current image of the subregion. The definition distinguishes the model field and its integral from any measured mass; it asserts no conservation, no positivity law of nature and no empirical value.

swept region ([[def-cm-continuum-motion]]).

$$\rho:U\longrightarrow(0,\infty)$$

whose physical reading is mass per unit volume: its dimension is
$[\rho]=\mu\ell^{-3}$ ([[def-cm01-units]], [[def-cm17-continuum-body-and-units]]).

is of class $C^1$ on $U$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]);

items.title: Adopted mass balance: the mass of every material subregion is constant in time
items.design_state: authored; step-1 readiness recorded in the batch notes
items.physical_scope: Adoption of mass conservation for a closed continuum model: for every material subregion and every time in the window, the model mass integral over the current image of the subregion is constant. The postulate excludes open systems, diffusion or exchange of material between labels, chemical reactions, phase change and mass sources; it asserts no empirical law and no measured value, and the local continuity equation is a theorem conditional on it.

references.title: R. Abeyaratne, Continuum Mechanics, Volume II of Lecture Notes on the Mechanics of Solids (MIT, 1988, revised 2020), Section 4.2 (the principle of conservation of mass and its local form)
K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Classical Mechanics (September 1, 2026 complete volume), Section 8.3 (continuity equation of a continuum)

items.statement:
Adopt the following assumption for every model of the continuum kinematic
branch of [[post-cm17-continuum-kinematic-model]] with density field of
[[def-cm17-density-and-mass]].

**(i) Mass balance.** Let $\chi$ be a motion of the model on the time window
$I$, let $J_0\subseteq I$ be an open interval with $\overline{J_0}\subseteq I$,
and let $B'\subseteq B$ be a material subregion (nonempty bounded open with
$\overline{B'}\subseteq B$). Then the model mass of $B'$,

$$m(t,B')=\int_{\chi_t(B')}\rho(t,x)\,dx\qquad(t\in J_0),$$

is constant in $t$:

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\chi_t(B')}\rho(t,x)\,dx=0\qquad(t\in J_0). \tag{CM}$$

The assumption is imposed for **every** material subregion and every time in
the window; the family of subregions is not restricted to a selected finite
list.

**(ii) Reading and exclusions.** The assumption says that a label carries its
matter permanently: the material of the body is a closed mechanical system
during the motion. It is **not** adopted, and no statement of this page
covers: open systems in which material is added to or removed from the body;
diffusion, mixing or relative transport of distinct constituents between
labels; chemical reactions, phase change or mass exchange between
constituents; mass sources or sinks distributed in the body; and relativistic
mass-energy conversion. In such situations the balance above can fail and a
different balance with source terms is required.

items.title: The transport identity and the material derivative along label worldlines for the adopted continuum model
items.design_state: authored; step-1 readiness recorded in the batch notes
items.physical_scope: Conditional on the adopted continuum kinematic model (smooth motion with positive Jacobian) and on the Axiom of Countable Choice used by the cited change-of-variables theorem: for a C^1 spatial field on a neighbourhood of the swept region of a body over a compactly contained time interval, the rate of change of the field's integral over the current image of the body equals the integral of the local time derivative plus the flux term div(fu); and along the worldline of a label the ordinary time derivative of the material field equals the material derivative D_tf = partial_t f + grad f . u. The theorem asserts no balance law and no empirical value.

([[def-countable-choice]]), as used by the transport theorem cited below. Let
$(B,O,I)$ be body data of [[def-cm17-continuum-body-and-units]], let $\chi$ be
a motion of the model on $I$ with spatial velocity $u$ and material
acceleration $a=D_tu$ ([[post-cm17-continuum-kinematic-model]],
[[def-cm-continuum-motion]]). Let $J_0\subseteq I$ be an open interval with
$\overline{J_0}\subseteq I$, put $\Sigma:=\{(t,x):t\in\overline{J_0},\
x\in\chi_t(\overline B)\}$, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^1$ on an
open set $U\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^3$ containing $\Sigma$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Then:

**(i) Transport identity.** The function $F(t):=\int_{\chi_t(B)}f(t,x)\,dx$ is
defined and differentiable on $J_0$, and for every $t\in J_0$

$$F'(t)=\int_{\chi_t(B)}\bigl(\partial_tf+\operatorname{div}(fu)\bigr)(t,x)\,dx .$$

The identity holds componentwise for a $C^1$ vector field $f$.

description of a material field $F_{\mathrm m}(t,X):=f(t,\chi(t,X))$, then for

of (i) is $D_tf+f\operatorname{div}u$ at the corresponding current point.

items.design_state: authored; step-1 readiness recorded in the batch notes
items.physical_scope: Conditional on the adopted mass-balance postulate, the smooth kinematic model and the Axiom of Countable Choice used by the transport machinery: conservation of the model mass of every material subregion is equivalent to the partial differential equation partial_t rho + div(rho u) = 0 on the current regions; equivalently the material derivative satisfies D_t rho = -rho div u, the product rho times the Jacobian is constant along each label worldline, the relative volume rate is div u, and the incompressibility condition div u = 0 is equivalent to the density being constant along each worldline in this branch. The theorem is a conditional model deduction and asserts no empirical value.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(B,O,I)$ be body data
([[def-cm17-continuum-body-and-units]]), let $\chi$ be a motion of the model
with spatial velocity $u$ ([[post-cm17-continuum-kinematic-model]],
[[def-cm-continuum-motion]]), let $J_0\subseteq I$ be an open interval with
$\overline{J_0}\subseteq I$, let $\Sigma$ be the swept region over
$\overline{J_0}$, and let $\rho:U\to(0,\infty)$ be a density field of class
$C^1$ on an open set $U$ containing $\Sigma$
([[def-cm17-density-and-mass]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]).
Assume the mass-balance postulate (CM) of [[post-cm17-mass-balance]] for every
material subregion and every $t\in J_0$. Then:

**(i) Local form.** For every $(t,x)\in J_0\times\chi_t(B)$,

$$\partial_t\rho(t,x)+\operatorname{div}\bigl(\rho u\bigr)(t,x)=0 . \tag{C}$$

Conversely, if (C) holds on an open neighbourhood of $\Sigma$, then (CM)
holds for every material subregion and every $t\in J_0$.

**(ii) Material form.** On $J_0\times\chi_t(B)$ the material derivative of the
density satisfies

$$D_t\rho=-\rho\operatorname{div}u ,$$

and writing $J(t,X)=\det D_X\chi_t(X)$ along the motion, the product
$\rho\bigl(t,\chi(t,X)\bigr)J(t,X)$ is constant in $t$ for every label
$X\in B$.

**(iii) Volume rate.** For every $X\in B$ and $t\in J_0$ one has
$\partial_tJ(t,X)=J(t,X)\operatorname{div}u(t,\chi(t,X))$: the relative rate of
change of an infinitesimal material volume is $\operatorname{div}u$, and the
identity of (ii) is the statement that density times volume is conserved
along a label.

$S^2=\{n\in\mathbb R^3:\|n\|_2=1\}$ be the unit sphere.

$$t:U\times S^2\longrightarrow\mathbb R^3,$$

force per unit area exerted **by the material on the side towards which $n$
points upon the material on the other side**, at the point $x$ of a surface
whose unit normal is $n$, at time $s$. Its dimension is that of force per

items.design_state: authored; step-1 readiness recorded in the batch notes
items.physical_scope: Adoption of the force description of the continuum branch: a continuous body-force field per unit mass on the swept region and a continuous traction field, force per unit area, depending on a contact surface only through its unit normal at the point (Cauchy's hypothesis). ([[post-cm17-continuum-kinematic-model]]) the following description of the
forces acting on the body, read in the fixed inertial frame and with the
dimensions of [[def-cm17-continuum-body-and-units]].

$b:U\to\mathbb R^3$ on an open set $U$ containing the swept region of the
motion over its time window, the **body force per unit mass**, of dimension

admissible region $D$ is $\int_D\rho b\,dx$, of dimension $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$

items.title: Adopted balance principles of the continuum model: force and couple-free torque balance on every admissible region
items.design_state: authored; step-1 readiness recorded in the batch notes
items.physical_scope: Adoption of the balance principles of the continuum branch in force form: on every admissible bounded piecewise C-one region inside the current region, the surface traction resultant balances minus the volume integral of the body force minus the inertial term rho a, and the corresponding torque about any fixed origin balances likewise with no body or surface couples. items.title: Existence, uniqueness and symmetry of the stress matrix from the adopted balance principles
items.design_state: authored; step-1 readiness recorded in the batch notes
items.physical_scope: Conditional on the adopted force model and balance principles: on every bounded spatial region inside the current configuration the continuous traction field is represented by a unique continuous stress matrix, the reversed-normal identity t(-n) = -t(n) holds, and the couple-free torque balance forces the stress matrix to be symmetric. The result is a conditional deduction from the adopted balance principles and the cited mathematical Cauchy-tetrahedron and angular-balance theorems; it asserts no positivity, no constitutive relation and no measured stress.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), as used by the surface and divergence machinery of
the cited theorems. Let the model and its fields be as in
[[post-cm17-momentum-balance]]: a motion $\chi$ with current regions
$\Omega_s$, a continuous density field $\rho$, spatial velocity $u$ and
material acceleration $a=D_tu$, a continuous body-force field $b$ and a
continuous traction field $t$, with the balance principles (F) and (T) of
that postulate holding for every admissible region at every time $s$.

Then for every time $s$ and every bounded open set $W\subseteq\Omega_s$ with
$\overline W$ contained in the open domain of the fields at time $s$ there is
a unique continuous matrix field

$$\sigma(s,\cdot):W\longrightarrow M_3(\mathbb R)$$

such that

$$t(s,y,n)=\sigma(s,y)\,n\qquad\text{for every }(y,n)\in W\times S^2 ,$$

and necessarily

$$t(s,y,-n)=-t(s,y,n)\qquad\bigl((y,n)\in W\times S^2\bigr),\qquad \sigma(s,y)^{\mathsf T}=\sigma(s,y)\qquad(y\in W).$$

The stress matrix is continuous and unique per time; positivity of its
isotropic part, a constitutive relation and any measured stress are **not**
asserted.

items.title: The momentum equation of the continuum model: local form rho D_t u = rho b + div sigma

The result is a conditional model deduction; it asserts no existence of solutions, no constitutive relation and no measured value.

[[post-cm17-linear-elastic-constitutive]] with reference density
$\rho_0>0$ and moduli $\lambda,\mu_s$ with $\mu_s>0$ and
$\lambda+\tfrac{2\mu_s}{3}>0$, and let

$$c_L:=\sqrt{\frac{\lambda+2\mu_s}{\rho_0}},\qquad \xi(t,x):=A\cos\bigl(\kappa x_1-\omega t\bigr)\,e_1,\qquad \omega:=\kappa c_L,$$

with $A\ne0$, $\kappa\ne0$ and $e_1$ the first standard basis vector: a
longitudinal plane wave travelling along $e_1$. Then:

1. the linear strain is $e_{11}(t,x)=-A\kappa\sin(\kappa x_1-\omega t)$ with
   all other entries zero, so $\operatorname{tr}e=e_{11}$ and
   $e_0=e-\tfrac13(\operatorname{tr}e)I_3$ has Frobenius squared norm
   $\tfrac23e_{11}^2$;
2. the stress matrix is
   $$\sigma(t,x)=(\lambda+2\mu_s)e_{11}(t,x)\,e_1e_1^{\mathsf T}+\lambda e_{11}(t,x)\,(e_2e_2^{\mathsf T}+e_3e_3^{\mathsf T});$$
3. the displacement equation (E) of
   [[pthm-cm17-linear-elastic-equation-of-motion]] with $b\equiv0$ holds
   exactly: $\rho_0\partial_t^2\xi_1=(\lambda+2\mu_s)\partial_1^2\xi_1$;
4. the strain-energy density is
   $W(e)=(\tfrac\lambda2+\mu_s)e_{11}^2=\mu_s\tfrac23e_{11}^2
   +(\tfrac\lambda2+\tfrac{\mu_s}3)e_{11}^2\ge0$, with equality only where
   $e_{11}=0$; both coefficients in the decomposition are positive under the
   branch's hypotheses, and the squared speed
   $c_L^2=(\lambda+2\mu_s)/\rho_0$ is positive with $[c_L]=\ell\tau^{-1}$.

items.physical_scope: A worked steady plane channel problem of the adopted incompressible Newtonian branch: the Poiseuille profile with pressure gradient 6, height 2 and viscosity 3 is verified against the model's momentum equation with zero body force, its flux per unit width 4/3 and centre speed 1 are computed, the Couette profile is verified with its nonzero curl, and the no-slip wall conditions are recorded as adopted ideal boundary data. The example reports no measurement.

references.title: K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Classical Mechanics (September 1, 2026 complete volume), Section 8.5 (Couette and Poiseuille flows with no-slip conditions)
R. Abeyaratne, Continuum Mechanics, Volume II of Lecture Notes on the Mechanics of Solids (MIT, 1988, revised 2020), Problems 12.9 and 12.14 (channel flows of the incompressible viscous model)

items.statement:
Adopt the incompressible Newtonian branch of [[post-cm17-fluid-constitutive]]
with constant density $\rho>0$, dynamic viscosity $\eta=3$ and the
two-dimensional channel $O=\mathbb R\times(0,2)\times\mathbb R$ with
coordinates $(x,y,z)$, in the steady description and with no body force, so
that by [[pthm-cm17-momentum-equation]] the branch's momentum equation reads
$\rho(u\cdot\nabla)u=-\nabla p+\eta\Delta u$ together with
$\operatorname{div}u=0$ ([[def-cm-fluid-constitutive-models]]). Then:

1. **(Poiseuille.)** With pressure gradient $G=6$, i.e.
   $p(x)=p_0-6x$, the profile
   $u=(v(y),0,0)$, $v(y)=y(2-y)$ (the value $Gh^3/(12\eta)$ of the general
   formula with $h=2,\eta=3$) satisfies $\operatorname{div}u=0$ and
   $\eta v''(y)=-6=-G$, hence the steady momentum equation with no body
   force; it satisfies the no-slip data $v(0)=v(2)=0$; its flux per unit
   width is $\int_0^2v(y)\,dy=4/3$ and its centre speed is $v(1)=1$.
2. **(Couette.)** With constant pressure and $V=2$, the profile
   $v(y)=Vy/2=y$ satisfies the same equations with zero body force and the
   boundary data $v(0)=0$, $v(2)=2$; its velocity gradient
   $D u=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&0\\0&0&0\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix}$ is not symmetric, so
   the flow is not irrotational: $\operatorname{curl}u=(0,0,-V/h)=(0,0,-1)$.
3. **(Uniqueness in the ansatz.)** Within the ansatz
   $u=(v(y),0,0)$, $p=p_0-Gx$, the difference of two profiles with the same
   $G$ and the same no-slip data satisfies $w''=0$ with $w(0)=w(2)=0$, hence
   $w\equiv0$: the Poiseuille profile is the unique steady solution in this
   class with those data.

items.statement:
Work on the periodic cell $\mathbb T^3=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^3$ of
[[post-cm17-fluid-constitutive]] clause (c), with constant density $\rho>0$,
no body force and the stress of the branch. Let $A>0$, $\varphi\in\mathbb R$
and

$$u(t,x):=\bigl(A\sin(2\pi x_2+\varphi),0,0\bigr).$$

Then:

1. $\operatorname{div}u=0$ and $(u\cdot\nabla)u=0$, so with $p\equiv0$ the
   field is an exact steady solution of the **Euler** branch ($\nu=0$) of the
   model on the periodic cell: $\partial_tu+P((u\cdot\nabla)u)=\nu\Delta u$
   holds as $0=0$, and the primitive equation
   $\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u=-\nabla p+\nu\Delta u$ holds with $p\equiv0$;
2. the field satisfies the hypotheses of
   [[pthm-cm17-incompressible-periodic-local-evolution]]: it is smooth,
   divergence-free, periodic and has finite $H^s$ norm ($s\ge4$), and the
   displayed global solution is consistent with the local
   existence-uniqueness statement;
3. for the **viscous** branch ($\nu>0$) the field is **not** a solution:
   $\Delta u=(2\pi)^2u\ne0$ and $P\Delta u=\Delta u$ because $u$ is
   divergence-free, so the projected equation would require
   $\nu\cdot(2\pi)^2u=0$, which fails for $A>0$;
4. more generally, every steady periodic shear $u=(v(x_2),0,0)$ of the
   viscous branch with no body force and constant density is **constant**:
   the model's equations force $\nabla p=\eta(v''(x_2),0,0)$, and periodicity
   of $p$ in $x_1$ together with periodicity of $v$ in $x_2$ forces
   $v''\equiv0$ and then $v\equiv\mathrm{const}$.

items.title: FALSE: the reversed-normal convention alone makes a continuous traction field a stress matrix. The field t(n)=|n_1|n refutes it
items.reference: batch-33 B page; constructed from the A-page statements
items.design_state: authored; step-1 readiness recorded in the batch notes

references.title: R. Abeyaratne, Continuum Mechanics, Volume II of Lecture Notes on the Mechanics of Solids (MIT, 1988, revised 2020), Section 4.3 (Cauchy's hypothesis and the need for force balance in the tetrahedron argument)
MIT OpenCourseWare 12.005, Applications of Continuum Mechanics, Lecture 3 (Cauchy tetrahedron and Cauchy's formula t = sigma n)

items.statement:
The false statement is: *every continuous traction field
$t:S^2\to\mathbb R^3$ satisfying the reversed-normal convention
$t(-n)=-t(n)$ for every $n\in S^2$ is represented by a matrix
$\sigma\in M_3(\mathbb R)$ with $t(n)=\sigma n$ for every $n$.*

The field constructed below is continuous and satisfies the convention, and
inherits Cauchy's hypothesis (it depends on the surface only through the unit
normal), but no matrix represents it. The refutation shows that the balance
hypothesis of the Cauchy-tetrahedron theorem is essential: symmetry of the
traction in the normal alone is not enough.
